content.comment_body: Good afternoon. This is my first time using this forum and I have a few questions. I need help limiting the values that a user can enter in the [product_name] Viewer; specifically, I want users to only be able to input values between 0 and 350. Currently, the input field allows any value between -20000 and +20000, and I am unable to restrict this range. Is it possible to set such a limit? If so, could someone explain how to do it, or provide an example? Another question: Is it possible to block all standard screens in [product_name], and show only the screens I created in my project? For instance, I want to remove the IO, Setup, Network, and Data screens, displaying only those that are part of the programmed interface. Is this feasible? If so, I'd appreciate instructions or an example. I look forward to your response and thank you for your attention.

1.) One possible solution is attached. The value entered by the user is checked against the 0 to 350 range. If it falls within this range, the value is accepted; otherwise, the system sets it to 0. 2.) It is not possible to block access to the default menu screens. Switching from administrator to operator mode will restrict access to certain system menu items, but this requires entering a password (by default, it is [product_name]). When switching back to administrator mode, all menu options become available again.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is seeking ways to restrict data input ranges and customize the visible screens on the [product_name] HMI. They want more control over input validation and the ability to personalize the HMI interface, but current product options limit menu configuration and do not support hiding core system screens entirely.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes to directly limit input ranges via the HMI and fully customize which screens are visible, so that only application-specific interfaces are exposed to the end user.
